answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and registers one willow-fibre paper batch, stamped with a violet watermark and an onyx seal hash on a board. Auditors recompute the watermark from batch and seal; a missing batch, reused seal, or mismatch burns the bond. The first same-funder batch costs 28 and the kth costs 28+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6022 and 1000 fake batches cost 3,025,000 plus 70,000 locked. Mills stamp at most 3 batches per epoch. A rented-mill ring fails because one shared seal across keys is exposed by recomputation. An honest agent pays 28 once and reclaims its bond.
